vulnerable.title: Vulnerable Configuration (Capital One 2019 State)
vulnerable.description: EC2 instance running ModSecurity reverse proxy with open SSRF forwarding, IMDSv1 enabled (no token required), and an IAM role with full administrative S3 permissions (s3:* on all resources).

Statement.SecurityComment: CRITICAL FLAW: Wildcard permission allows the WAF instance to execute ListAllMyBuckets, GetObject, and PutObject across every single S3 bucket in the AWS account.
CRITICAL FLAW: No aws:sourceVpce condition or KMS encryption key boundary. Any principal with s3:GetObject can read the files.

ssrf_defense_config.explanation: Incoming reverse proxy forwards queries to any supplied URL without filtering link-local addresses (169.254.169.254) or RFC1918 private subnets.

secured.title: Secured Configuration (Remediated CloudGuard State)
secured.description: Multi-layered defense: SSRF filter blocks link-local/RFC1918 targets, IMDSv2 enforces session tokens (PUT handshake with hop-limit=1), IAM role follows Least Privilege with explicit deny on sensitive data, and S3 bucket restricts access strictly to VPC Endpoints.

Statement.SecurityComment: SECURED: WAF role is tightly scoped strictly to writing its own operational logs.
SECURED: Explicit DENY always overrides any Allow statements in IAM evaluation logic.
SECURED: Requests originating outside the designated VPC Endpoint are unconditionally denied.

ssrf_defense_config.explanation: Strict URL validation whitelist and socket connection interception. Metadata service link-local address is completely unreachable via proxy.
